q: For STERILE WRAPPED surgical packs in a gravity-displacement autoclave, the standard steam parameter is:
e: Wrapped: 121°C (250°F), ~15 min, 15 psi. Unwrapped/flash: 132°C (270°F), 3–4 min.

q: Chemical indicator reacting to all critical steam variables?
e: Class 5 integrators track time, temperature, and steam penetration.

q: Biological indicator organism for steam autoclave validation?
e: G. stearothermophilus spores are the steam gold standard (B. atrophaeus is for dry heat/EtO).

q: Minimum recommended frequency for biological spore testing?
e: Weekly is commonly cited; confirm against ASV Standards of Care.

q: Best suture for a 4-month kitten's subcutis (rapid absorption, low drag)?
e: Monocryl hydrolyzes fast and is low-reaction.

q: Why is braided Vicryl discouraged for skin/fascia in high-risk patients?
o: Capillarity wicks bacteria into the site
e: Braided multifilament wicks bacteria.

q: Best suture for linea alba in a mature large-breed dog?
e: PDS retains tensile strength longest (~6 weeks).

q: Pedicle (autoligation) tie is most safely used in:
e: Standard on feline ovarian pedicles; avoid large/deep-chested dogs.

q: Adult bitch in deep estrus at an open shelter for spay. Best timing?
o: Proceed now; delay increases LOS and disease exposure
e: Welfare risk of prolonged stay outweighs estrus engorgement.

q: Minimum barrier between a clean prep table and an unsterile dental station in one room?
o: Physically separate room or enclosed alcove
e: Dental scaling aerosolizes pathogens; isolate clean surgery.

q: Halsted's gentle handling reduces which mediators of pain/edema?
e: Less cell lysis limits the arachidonic-acid cascade.

q: Sterilization alternative for heat/moisture-sensitive instruments?
e: Gas plasma sterilizes without toxic residue (10-min glutaraldehyde is only disinfection).

q: Most reliable sterile shelf-life wrap configuration?
e: Double sequential wrap creates a tortuous barrier path.

q: Feral cat in a trap needs restraint + visceral analgesia + reversibility. Best combo?
e: DKT gives restraint, somatic+visceral analgesia, partial reversibility.

q: Mechanism of dexmedetomidine bradycardia?
e: High afterload triggers baroreceptor reflex bradycardia.

q: Dexmed-pretreated patient: HR 42, pink MM, high MAP. Correct action?
o: No anticholinergic; reverse with atipamezole only if perfusion fails
e: Forcing HR up against vasoconstriction overloads the myocardium; perfusion is adequate here.

q: Which agent provides NO analgesia?
e: Phenothiazines tranquilize but give zero analgesia.

q: Why is acepromazine contraindicated in a dehydrated dog with pale MM?
e: Acepromazine vasodilation worsens hypotension in hypovolemia.

q: Why are puppies <8 weeks sensitive to hepatically/renally cleared drugs?
e: Immature metabolism/clearance prolongs half-lives.

q: Fastest indicator of ET tube disconnection/obstruction?
e: Capnography flatlines immediately.

q: Capnograph baseline ETCO2 climbs to 55 mmHg. Action?
e: Elevated ETCO2 = respiratory acidosis from hypoventilation.

q: Minimum MAP to autoregulate renal/cerebral perfusion?
e: Below 60 mmHg risks ischemic organ damage.

q: Why does SpO2 92% on 100% oxygen need evaluation?
e: Expect 98–100% on oxygen; 92% = hypoxemia.

q: Why avoid chamber induction with isoflurane?
e: Chamber induction panics patients and contaminates the room.

q: Why are electric heating pads prohibited in recovery?
o: Sedated patients cannot move from heat points → burns
e: Thermoregulation failure plus immobility causes burns.

q: Severe intra-op haemorrhage: capnograph change?
e: Falling cardiac output reduces CO2 delivery to lungs.

q: When should a 6-week pup at a high-density shelter start core vaccines?
e: Intake vaccination counters immediate exposure risk.

q: Why prefer MLV core vaccines in shelters?
o: Rapid response and can overcome low MDA
e: Rapid robust protection in high-exposure settings.

q: Main cause of vaccine failure in a pup boosted q3 wk to 12 wk?
e: MDA can block vaccines to 16–20 weeks.

q: 3-yo intact male cat, no vaccine history. Core protocol?
o: FVRCP at intake + booster 2–4 wk later
e: Naive adults need a priming dose plus one booster 2–4 weeks later.

q: Which MLV vaccine risks fetal cerebellar hypoplasia in pregnant queens?
e: MLV FPV damages the developing fetal cerebellum.

q: Unvaccinated shelter dog bites staff, breaks skin. Mandate?
o: Observe 10 days; do not vaccinate in the window
e: 10-day observation confirms infectious virus in saliva at the bite.

q: Why are adjuvanted vaccines more linked to FISS?
e: Persistent adjuvant inflammation transforms feline fibroblasts.

q: What does Capacity for Care (C4C) define?
o: Quality care to every animal, matching needs to staff/space/mandate
e: C4C balances holding with staff bandwidth and medical capability.

q: Benchmark surgeries per HQHVSN surgeon per day (practical, not ASV)?
e: Practical benchmark (Sara White), not an ASV standard.

q: Practical minimum body weight commonly used for pediatric SN?
e: ~1 kg / 2 lb is a practical floor; ASV early-age window is 6–16 weeks.

q: Cornerstone analgesic class after elective orchiectomy in an active dog?
e: NSAIDs give stable long-lasting control for routine elective surgery.

q: Why discourage routine prophylactic post-op antibiotics for clean SN?
o: Clean surgery does not benefit; overuse drives resistance
e: Stewardship reserves prophylaxis for contaminated/infected fields.

q: Most sensitive indicator of acute post-op pain in a non-verbal patient?
o: Guarding, abnormal posture, vocalizing on palpation
e: Objective behavioral change is the most sensitive marker.

q: Maximum lidocaine dose for a testicular block in DOGS (standard reference)?
e: Dogs tolerate ~6–10 mg/kg; cats far less (~2–4). Std-ref range.

q: Over-inflated ET cuff in a cat: localized complication?
e: Feline tracheas are sensitive to over-inflation injury.

q: Primary purpose of an active gas scavenging system?
o: Remove waste anaesthetic gas to protect staff
e: Limits chronic trace anaesthetic exposure.

q: Feline spay line: sloped loss of capnograph waveform. Why check the ET tube?
o: Viscous mucus can occlude small tubes
e: Small feline tubes are prone to mucus plugs.

q: Per the ASPCA reference, which disinfectant is NOT reliably effective against non-enveloped parvovirus?
e: Quats are not effective vs non-enveloped viruses per independent research.

q: Why avoid stiff bristles/scraping during surgical skin prep?
e: Gentle prep preserves the epidermal barrier.

q: ASV spay-neuter standard for instrument maintenance?
o: Documented schedule for sharpening, alignment, ultrasonic cleaning
e: Documented routine maintenance ensures reliable performance.

q: First-line drug for acute anaphylaxis to a vaccine or anaesthetic?
e: Epinephrine is the gold standard.

q: Halsted: obliterating dead space primarily prevents:
e: Seroma is an ideal medium for bacterial growth.

q: "Targeting by income" in HQHVSN means:
e: Area-based location and pricing, not screening.

q: Leading relinquishment risk that HQHVSN targeting addresses?
e: Intact status is the leading relinquishment risk.

q: Pediatric (6–16 wk) fasting before surgery?
o: Small meal 2–4 h pre-op; not >4 h
e: Prevents hypoglycemia.

q: Owned pets best scheduled at 4 months mainly to:
e: The 4-month figure relates to vaccination/immunity.

q: Intubation of cats for procedures under 30 minutes:
o: Acceptable to omit if emergency equipment available
e: CEPSAF: feline intubation is not benign; omission acceptable with backup.

q: Which monitor reduces anaesthetic death risk in cats?
e: Pulse oximetry (CEPSAF) lowers feline anaesthetic death risk.

q: Jaw tone is unreliable for depth in:
e: Pediatric puppies lack mandibular tone.

q: En bloc gravid uterus removal: fetal euthanasia is:
o: Not necessary unless the sac is opened
e: Fetuses stay unconscious unless the sac is opened.

q: Recommended permanent identifier for a neutered community cat?
e: Ear tip (one-third distal pinna, perpendicular) is the standard; notching discouraged.

q: Sterile gloves are required for:
o: All abdominal surgery and adult dog castration
e: Exam gloves OK for routine cat/puppy castration; sterile for abdominal and adult dog castration.

q: Most post-op complications occur within:
e: First 3 hours is the critical window.

q: Recommended perioperative ambient temperature range?
e: Thermostat low-to-mid 70s°F (low-to-mid 20s°C) typical.

q: Which scavenging method is specifically discouraged by ASV?
e: Charcoal canister scavenging is discouraged.

q: Contagious-but-eligible animals should be scheduled:
e: Operate suspected-contagious animals last.

q: Partial alpha-2 reversal in a multimodal protocol:
e: Shortens recovery while preserving analgesia.

q: NSAIDs should be avoided in SN patients that are:
e: Dehydration raises nephrotoxicosis risk.

q: Which model offers the greatest daily surgical capacity?
e: Stationary clinics have the highest daily capacity.

q: Recommended ergonomic micropauses during surgery?
e: Short frequent micropauses cut fatigue and raise accuracy.

q: Median survival time of spayed female cats vs intact is best stated as:
e: MST is a duration (~13.1 yr); the "13.1%" was a transcription error.

q: A positive point-of-care LH test in a cat is consistent with:
e: Loss of gonadal negative feedback raises LH after neutering. Test stats are source-specific.

q: In dogs, cryptorchid testes are roughly how much more likely to become neoplastic?
e: Reported ~9.2–13.6×; source-specific.

q: Representative dexmedetomidine premed range in CATS (std ref)?
e: ~0.02–0.04 mg/kg IM in cats; dogs are lower per kg. Std-ref range.

q: How is atipamezole dosed to reverse dexmedetomidine?
o: The same volume as the dexmed given, IM
e: Give an equal volume to the dexmedetomidine, IM; avoid IV except emergencies.

q: Bupivacaine must never be given by which route?
e: Bupivacaine is cardiotoxic IV.

q: Local technique that reduces nociception and inhalant need during castration?
e: Intratesticular local block blunts the spermatic-cord stimulus.

q: Correct meloxicam regimen for a healthy adult dog post-spay?
e: Meloxicam dog: ~0.2 mg/kg load then 0.1 mg/kg; cats single dose with caution. Std-ref.

q: AAHA-recommended STARTING anaesthetic IV fluid rate in dogs?
e: AAHA 2013: start ~5 (dog)/3 (cat) mL/kg/h, titrate down; older standard was 10. Std-ref.

q: Which patients DO warrant IV fluids per ASV?
o: Pregnant, pyometra, blood loss, prolonged surgery
e: ASV reserves IV fluids for high-risk patients; routine electives often need none.

q: Propofol induction dose in a WELL-PREMEDICATED dog?
e: Premedication lowers propofol need to ~2–4 mg/kg titrated.

q: Anticholinergic appropriate for VAGAL (not alpha-2) bradycardia?
e: Atropine/glycopyrrolate for vagal bradycardia; never for alpha-2 bradycardia.

q: Per the ASPCA reference, household bleach dilution and contact time effective against parvovirus?
e: 1:32 (about half a cup per gallon, ~120 mL per 3.8 L), 10-minute contact on precleaned surfaces.

q: Per the ASPCA reference, diluted stability of accelerated hydrogen peroxide?
e: Accelerated H2O2 is stable ~90 days diluted (potassium peroxymonosulfate ~7 days; bleach ~24 h).

q: Per the ASPCA reference, which two agents are most inactivated by organic matter and need a rinse?
e: Bleach and calcium hypochlorite are organic-matter sensitive, need extensive precleaning and a rinse.

q: The hardest resource to obtain when setting up a program (ASV)?
e: ASV identifies funding as the hardest resource.

q: For a program to stay accessible, fees for service must be:
e: Accessibility requires fees below local GP prices; shortfall covered by efficiency/volunteers/funding.

q: Effective HQHVSN work culture is best described as:
e: Collaborative teamwork correlates with fewer complications.

q: Program EFFECTIVENESS is measured by:
o: Local intake/euthanasia rates, complaints, colony size, kitten production
e: Population-level metrics gauge whether targeting is working.

q: Which opioid gives the longest analgesia and is a good feline take-home (OTM) option?
e: Buprenorphine (~6–8 h) suits feline take-home; butorphanol is short-acting; acepromazine has no analgesia.

q: Benchmark daily surgical volume for a sustainable stationary HQHVSN clinic (one vet)?
e: About 35 surgeries per vet per day, 5 days/week, 48 weeks/year. Source-specific planning figure.

q: Catchment commonly cited as needed to sustain a stationary clinic?
e: ~250,000 people within ~60 miles (97 km), plus about a $35,000 opening reserve. Source-specific.

q: Fastest, lowest-cost way to start an HQHVSN program?
e: MASH clinics have the lowest setup cost and suit both rural and dense urban areas.

q: In a collaborative MASH model, the host organisation typically provides:
e: Hosts supply venue/personnel/scheduling; the MASH org supplies vets, techs, surgical supplies and training.

q: Recommended HQHVSN staff ratio (vet to trained support)?
e: About one vet to two or three trained support staff; 4x10 h or 3x12 h shifts work better than 5x8 h.

q: CEPSAF anaesthetic mortality in healthy elective cats (ASA I to II)?
e: ~0.11% healthy cats vs ~1.4% sick cats; dogs ~0.05% vs ~1.33%.

q: Which change INCREASES MAC (needing more inhalant)?
e: Hyperthermia, hypernatraemia and CNS stimulants raise MAC; the others lower it.

q: A capnograph baseline that does not return to zero indicates:
o: Rebreathing CO2 (exhausted soda lime or stuck expiratory valve)
e: An elevated baseline means inspired CO2 is being rebreathed.

q: A 'curare cleft' on the capnograph plateau means:
o: The patient is breathing against the circuit (light plane or waning relaxant)
e: The cleft reflects spontaneous effort against the ventilator/circuit.

q: In a 6 to 12 week pediatric patient, cardiac output depends primarily on:
e: Non-compliant ventricles mean CO is rate-dependent, so bradycardia causes immediate hypotension.

q: RECOVER chest-compression rate?
e: 100 to 120/min, 1/3 to 1/2 chest width, full recoil.

q: RECOVER ventilation rate for an intubated arrest patient?
e: 10/min; hyperventilation raises intrathoracic pressure and crashes preload.

q: If epinephrine must be given intratracheally during CPR, the dose is:
e: Intratracheal epinephrine is 10x the IV dose, diluted for alveolar absorption.

q: Roughly how much isotonic crystalloid remains intravascular 30 to 60 min after a bolus?
e: About 25% stays intravascular (75% shifts interstitial), so over-hydration drives oedema.

q: Maximum acceptable time from clamping the uterine blood supply to delivery in en bloc caesarean?
e: 45 to 60 seconds; longer risks fetal hypoxia. One resuscitator per neonate.

q: Which caesarean technique gives the highest neonatal survival and shortest dam GA time?
o: En bloc OHE then hand-off hysterotomy
e: En bloc removal minimises dam GA time, contamination, and maximises neonatal survival.

q: Which neonatal resuscitation manoeuvre is NO LONGER recommended?
e: Swinging/shaking risks intracranial haemorrhage and head/neck injury.

q: Neonatal bradycardia during resuscitation is usually due to, and managed by:
e: Most neonatal bradycardia is hypoxic, so anticholinergics are not recommended; oxygenate first.

q: Ovary-sparing spay (hysterectomy keeping ovaries) still carries the risk of:
o: Pyometra (unless all uterine tissue to the cervix is removed)
e: Stump pyometra risk persists and estrus behaviour continues; all uterine tissue must be removed to avoid stump pyometra.

q: Tearing of the ovarian pedicle is more commonly associated with which side?
e: The right ovary is more cranial and harder to exteriorise.

q: Ovarian remnant syndrome is more common in which species, and is best resected when?
o: Cats; about 2 to 3 weeks after luteinisation or during behavioural estrus
e: ~0.3% cats vs ~0.04% dogs; operate when ovarian tissue is most identifiable (post-luteinisation or in estrus).

q: Recommended surgical approach for feline mammary fibroadenomatous hyperplasia?
e: Flank spay is recommended; the hyperplasia is progesterone-driven and regresses after ovariectomy.

q: Secondary post-spay haemorrhage from uterine-vessel erosion typically presents:
e: Often 4 to 16 days out; any serious vaginal bleed warrants immediate exploration and re-ligation.

q: Every spay/neuter patient should be discharged with which item to prevent dehiscence?
e: Self-trauma is the main cause of skin dehiscence; an E-collar is standard.

q: Preferred vasopressor to support blood pressure during caesarean (preserves uterine flow)?
e: Ephedrine maintains or improves uterine blood flow despite vasoconstriction.

q: Which anticholinergic does NOT cross the placenta (preferred for maternal bradycardia in caesarean)?
e: Glycopyrrolate's size/charge keep it out of fetal circulation; atropine crosses (and raises fetal HR).

q: The one sedative specifically linked to neonatal and maternal mortality (avoid in caesarean)?
e: Xylazine is the alpha-2 agonist associated with both neonatal and maternal mortality.

q: Most accurate monitor of sterilisation efficacy, run weekly?
e: Biological indicators (G. stearothermophilus for steam) are the most accurate; run weekly.

q: Most commonly used suture type in HQHVSN?
e: Synthetic monofilament absorbable (Monocryl, PDS) predominates.

q: Clipping the surgical site more than 4 hours before surgery does what to SSI risk?
e: Clipping well before surgery (or before induction) increases SSI risk roughly threefold.

q: Minimum thread count for woven cotton muslin sterilisation wrap?
e: Minimum ~140 thread count for muslin (270-count pima cotton is the barrier-equivalence benchmark).

q: Most effective surgical hand-prep agent?
e: Alcohol-based products are most effective, then chlorhexidine, then iodophors; brushless preferred.

q: When cleaning cages, which animals are cared for first?
e: Clean the most vulnerable first, then unknown-vaccination adults; pediatrics are also housed separately.

q: Why must many commercial gabapentin oral solutions be avoided in cats?
e: Xylitol-containing liquids are toxic to cats; use xylitol-free compounded liquid or capsules.

q: Typical canine pre-visit trazodone dose range?
e: ~4 to 12 mg/kg q8 to 12 h (start ~4 to 7 mg/kg); cats ~50 mg/cat.

q: Free-roaming cat population dynamics are MOST sensitive to:
e: Survival (especially adult) outweighs fecundity, which is why removal often beats equal-intensity sterilisation.

q: In population simulations, sterilising only male cats produced:
o: Essentially no change vs no sterilisation
e: Male-only sterilisation showed no meaningful population change.

q: Boone et al. (2019) modelling suggested effective TNR requires sterilising about:
e: ~75% of intact cats per 6-month interval to drive decline; non-surgical contraception needs >40 to 50% per 6 months plus limited migration.

q: Why is test-and-cull for FeLV/FIV discouraged in community cats?
o: High false-positive rate at low prevalence risks euthanising healthy cats
e: At low prevalence up to ~50% of positives can be false, risking euthanasia of uninfected cats.

q: Most common sex-chromosome disorder of sexual development in dogs and cats?
e: XXY (Klinefelter) is the most commonly reported.

q: Persistent Mullerian duct syndrome is hereditary in which breeds?
e: Miniature Schnauzers in the US, Basset Hounds in Europe; often cryptorchid.

q: A true hermaphrodite is defined by:
o: At least one ovary and one testis (or an ovotestis)
e: True hermaphrodite = both gonadal tissues present; pseudohermaphrodites have one gonad type with discordant phenotype.

q: In all confirmed disorders of sexual development, the recommendation is:
e: Gonadectomy is recommended in all DSD cases (neoplasia and welfare risk).

q: St. Tammany Parish substantially improved feline live outcomes — from 26% to over 95% — while operating under restrictive local ordinances. What is the primary lesson for shelter medicine practitioners?
o: Ordinance reform must precede any meaningful improvement in feline live outcomes
Shelters can achieve dramatic feline lifesaving improvements through programs and practices even before restrictive ordinances are changed
Live outcome improvements of this magnitude require regional collaboration across multiple parishes
TNR programs cannot succeed without explicit local legal authorization
e: The data showed that the major gains in live outcomes were achieved through operational programs and practices implemented despite restrictive ordinances — not as a result of ordinance revision. The ordinance changes had relatively little additional impact, though they were generally positive.

q: When St. Tammany Parish revised its ordinance to remove barriers to community cat management, what effect did this have on feline live outcomes?
o: It caused a temporary decline in live outcomes due to increased intake from community cat programs
It was associated with relatively little change, though it removed impoundment requirements and facilitated community cat programs
It produced the single largest year-over-year increase in live release rates
It had no measurable effect on intake or outcomes in the three-year review period
e: The abstract explicitly states that ordinance revision was 'associated with relatively little change' in outcomes. The major improvements had already occurred through programmatic changes. The ordinance changes were positive but not the main driver of lifesaving.

q: What is the authors' main conclusion about applying a Ricker model to TNR programs?
o: It is inappropriate for assessing TNR effectiveness
It is the gold standard for TNR
It accurately predicts cat population stability
e: The authors conclude the Ricker model is inappropriate for evaluating TNR effectiveness.

q: Why does the Ricker model fail for free-roaming cat populations?
o: It predicts wild population swings inconsistent with observed stability
e: The model predicts large population swings that don't match the relative stability of real free-roaming cat populations.

q: Which alternative model do the authors favor for predicting needed sterilization effort?
o: A stochastic model accounting for cat movement in and out
e: A stochastic model that accounts for immigration/emigration of cats is deemed better suited.
